thread:
pd-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: redwood-inference-canary service — triggered (critical). Alert: canary error-rate > 5% over 3m. Paging oncall.

incident-bot: Canary rollout (release:v2026-03-14-canary) detected elevated 5xxs from model-serving pool 'canary-us-west'. Metric: canary_p50_errors=6.4%. Traffic split 5%.

sam.k: acked — oncall here. looking now. which canary shard?

sasha: seeing spike across canary shards 3/4. stacktrace shows kvcache misses and kernel OOM logs in runtime. attaching excerpt:```
E 03:12:06 runtime: kv cache miss for key id=0x7f3a
E 03:12:07 GPU kernel oom abrt at ./kernel.c:223
```

sam.k: thanks. customer-facing? any user-facing 503s?

mzhao: yes, retro proxy logs show upstream 502/503 toward a subset of customers. estimated impacted requests ~4.8% globally, but two customers (acme-inc, healthlytics) with higher errors ~12% on some routes.

tara.cs: pinging customer-sre on impact. @customer-sre can you confirm whether any paid customers reported?

customer-sre: acme-inc opened a support ticket, they saw request failures and degraded latency. They've paused heavy flows. We should prioritize rollback or divert.

dev-ops: quick note — autoscaler didn't kick because canary pods hit OOM before readiness probe; new image contained a quant kernel change.

sam.k: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop traffic to canary (set traffic-split=0 for release:v2026-03-14-canary) 2) scale down canary replicas 3) roll back canary to previous image v2026-03-07-stable 4) monitor p50/p95 and error-rate for 30m.

sasha: I can flip traffic-split. doing `rbacctl deploy traffic-split set redwood-inference 0 --release v2026-03-14-canary` now.

sasha: done — traffic-split acknowledged, current split=0. Updating dashboard... :eyes:

incident-bot: Traffic-split change recorded by sasha at 03:18. Canary inbound traffic reduced to 0%.

mzhao: scaling canary down: `kubectl scale deploy canary-serving --replicas=0 -n inference` — running.

dev-ops: starting rollback: `deployctl rollback redwood-inference --to v2026-03-07-stable --strategy immediate`

sam.k: confirming rollback initiated. @tara.cs monitor customer ticket and confirm whether acme-inc resumes flows.

tara.cs: on it — I'm replying to acme-inc, letting them know we're rolling back and will follow up in 30m.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed (ack by sam.k).

incident-bot: Rollback completed at 03:27 by dev-ops. New active release: v2026-03-07-stable. Canary pods terminated.

mzhao: pre/post metrics: error-rate dropped to baseline within ~90s after rollback. current canary_error_rate=0.7%. p95 latency back to normal.

sasha: re-opening autoscaler ticket for kernel oom path. filing PR to add memory headroom and fail-fast for kernel allocation.

dev-ops: deploy artifact pinned to stable in router rules to avoid accidental canary reactivation.

sam.k: handing off to next oncall for follow-up: @tara.cs will run postmortem steps and coordinate with eng-runtime for root cause. I'm taking notes for incident timeline.

tara.cs: taking handoff. I'll run RCA, include logs, timeline, reproducible steps, and mitigation: Add canary gating and mem-check in CI.

customer-sre: acme-inc confirmed they retried and errors cleared after ~5 minutes. They're asking for a brief postmortem. I'll coordinate.

sam.k: thanks all. summary: canary image introduced quant kernel change that caused kernel OOMs -> pod crashes -> 5xxs for ~5% requests for 15m. mitigations: immediate traffic cut, scale down, rollback, pinned stable. Next: CI memory tests, canary slow ramp, alert tuning to include OOM traces.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: status=mitigated, severity=critical->resolved. Please file an incident report to /incidents/postmortems with timeline and action items. :white_check_mark: 

pd-bot: PagerDuty: incident cleared by sam.k at 03:32.

sam.k: closing thread; handoff complete.
